To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell density-mediated cellulase synthesis in C. ruminicola is regulated at the transcriptional level and that the transcriptional regulation of cellulase synthesis is controlled by the cell density-dependent catabolite repression.

(a) C. ruminicola produces cellulolytic enzymes at low cell density, (b) the cellulolytic enzyme production is regulated by the cell density, and (c) the cell density mediated regulation of cellulase synthesis is due to the repression of cellulase genes by the catabolite repressor protein CcpA.

C. ruminicola can be grown in a defined medium containing glucose as a carbon source, that the cellulolytic activity is induced in the culture by adding cellulose to the culture medium, and that the cellulase synthesis is cell density dependent, with the highest cellulase synthesis observed when the cell density reaches 2.0-3.0 x 10(8) cells/ml.
